//: P1-C05.2 (R109): steering wheels with pedals as host players, mapped by profile data. A wheel's DRIVE stick is steering (x) and accelerator minus brake (y); its ACTION stick comes from buttons (boost right, drift left, OI! up, cone down), so a wheel player is the same two-stick player as a pad (R60, R80). Gamepad API axes are -1..1; a pedal's 'rest' and 'full' are its axis value released and fully pressed (many wheels rest at +1 and read -1 at full travel). Wheels are matched by the USB vendor and product ids in the Gamepad id string. Axis layouts vary by model, driver and pedal mode (combined or separate), so a shipped profile is a starting point marked verified: false until someone confirms it on the device; the input drawer shows its live mapping, and its calibration maps any wheel and saves the result for that device (profiles in localStorage under jj.wheelProfiles.v1, which win over these).

profiles.label: Logitech G29 / G920
profiles.note: Separate-pedals mode: accelerator on the Y axis and brake on Rz (PCGamingWiki, MathWorks' G29 block), in the HID usage order Chromium gives axes (X 0, Y 1, Z 2, Rx 3, Ry 4, Rz 5). Paddles as boost and drift. Confirm on a device, or calibrate.
